title: Circuits & Network Theorems
summary: Expect 6–9 questions. Most are one-step numericals (Thevenin, max power, star–delta, 3-phase power, resonance) plus theorem conditions (linearity, bilateral).
definitions: KCL
Algebraic sum of currents at a node is zero (conservation of charge).
KVL
Algebraic sum of voltages around a closed loop is zero (conservation of energy).
Thevenin equivalent
V_{th} (open-circuit voltage) in series with R_{th} (resistance seen at the terminals with independent sources killed).
Norton equivalent
I_{N} (short-circuit current) in parallel with R_{N} = R_{th}.
Superposition
In a linear network, a response equals the sum of responses to each independent source acting alone (voltage sources shorted, current sources opened).
Reciprocity
In a linear bilateral network with one source, interchanging source and response positions leaves the ratio unchanged.
Resonance
Condition where X_{L} = X_{C}; the circuit is purely resistive and pf = 1.
Quality factor Q
Ratio of reactive to resistive energy; Q = ω_{0}L/R; sets selectivity.
Form factor
RMS ÷ average value (1.11 for a sine).
Peak (crest) factor
Peak ÷ RMS value (1.414 for a sine).
formulas: V = IR,  P = VI = I²R = V²/R
R_a = R_ab·R_ca/(R_ab + R_bc + R_ca); equal: R_Y = R_Δ/3
R_ab = R_a + R_b + R_a·R_b/R_c; equal: R_Δ = 3R_Y
Z = √(R² + (X_L − X_C)²),  pf = cos φ = R/Z
S = VI (VA),  P = VI cos φ (W),  Q = VI sin φ (VAR),  S² = P² + Q²
τ_RC = RC,  τ_RL = L/R;  v_C = V(1 − e^(−t/τ))
facts: Superposition cannot be used for power (power is not linear).
Efficiency at maximum power transfer is only 50% — power systems are designed for high efficiency, not max power transfer.
Series resonance: Z minimum, I maximum (acceptor circuit). Parallel resonance: Z maximum, line current minimum (rejector circuit).
Pure L: current lags 90°; pure C: current leads 90° (ELI the ICE man). Average power in pure L or C is zero.
Two-wattmeter: pf = 1 → readings equal; pf = 0.5 → one reads zero; pf < 0.5 → one reads negative.
Ideal voltage source has zero internal resistance; ideal current source has infinite internal resistance.
Capacitor = open circuit at DC steady state; inductor = short circuit.
Tellegen's theorem holds for ANY lumped network (linear or not) because it rests only on KCL and KVL.
traps: Two-wattmeter tan φ uses √3 × difference/sum — not the ratio of the readings.
Star line voltage = √3 × phase voltage, but line current = phase current. Don't mix with delta.
In 3-phase power use LINE values with √3, or PHASE values with 3 — never line values with 3.
Max power formula is V²/(4R), not V²/R or V²/(2R).
Z = 3 + j4 has pf = 0.6 (R/Z), not 0.8 (that is sin φ).

examples.q: 24 V source with 6 Ω internal resistance feeds a 12 Ω resistor. Find Thevenin equivalent across the 12 Ω and the maximum power to a load placed there.
Balanced load: V_L = 400 V, I_L = 10 A, pf 0.8 lagging. Find P, Q and S.
Series RLC: R = 10 Ω, L = 0.1 H, C = 10 µF. Find f0, Q and bandwidth.
